title: Where it grows
subtitle: The Mediterranean grape
objectives: Explain why old bush vines matter

steps.title: A wide map
steps.body: Grenache is one of the world's most planted red grapes. In France, it leads the southern Rhône and much of the Languedoc-Roussillon and Provence rosé. In Spain, it grows in Aragón, Navarra, Priorat, Rioja and around Madrid. Sardinia's Cannonau, Australia's Barossa and McLaren Vale, and California also grow it.

steps.title: Bush vines
steps.body: Grenache has strong, upright wood, so it's often grown as free-standing bush vines, gobelet. They need no trellis and withstand wind. Old bush vines, some over 100 years, with deep roots, survive drought and give low yields of concentrated fruit. Many of Grenache's best wines come from them.

steps.prompt: Match each place to its Grenache.
steps.explanation: Grenache thrives across warm, dry regions.

steps.title: Blending
steps.body: Grenache brings red fruit, body and alcohol to blends. Syrah adds colour and structure; Mourvèdre adds tannin and savoury notes; Carignan adds acidity. Rioja adds Garnacha to Tempranillo. Its low colour and tendency to oxidise make it a natural team player.

steps.explanation: Grenache ripens easily; it's rarely unripe.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Grenache is one of the most planted red grapes
Old bush vines give concentrated wines
It's a team player in GSM and Rioja blends
